newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2914 on Tuesday from Monday's 8.2925 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai due to active buying whenever it slipped below the 8.2920 resistance level, traders said.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2916.

The yuan opened higher at 8.2919 and moved stably in a range between 8.2916 and 8.2913 for most of the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2911 and a low of 8.2928. Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2914, traders said.
One dealer said buying was active whenever the yuan slipped below 8.2920, indicating pro-yuan sentiment was strong.
"This buying supported the yuan today, indicating pro-yuan sentiment is strong," he said. "But buyers seem to have no intention to push up the rate to the key 8.2900 resistance level."
A second dealer said the yuan moved in a more stable way on Tuesday after wide flunctuations in the past two days.
"After the yuan closed at a two-year high last Friday and fell sharply on Monday, it moved more steadily today," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around 8.2920 on Wednesday.
The yuan closed down at 7.2511 from 7.1770 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0692 from 1.0704 against the Hong Kong dollar.
